items.prompt:
Read the two sentences. Which one is formal and which one is informal?
A) 'The rainforest is a fascinating ecosystem with many diverse species.'
B) 'The rainforest is like super cool and has tons of animals!'
items.answer: A is formal. B is informal.

steps: A uses precise vocabulary ('fascinating ecosystem,' 'diverse species') and no slang — formal.
B uses casual words ('like super cool,' 'tons of') and an exclamation — informal.

items.prompt:
Which sentence would be appropriate for a class report?
A) 'Elephants are huge and they eat a lot of plants and stuff.'
B) 'Elephants are large herbivores that consume many types of plants.'
items.answer: B) 'Elephants are large herbivores that consume many types of plants.'

steps: A class report requires formal language.
B uses precise vocabulary: 'herbivores,' 'consume,' no slang.
A has informal phrases: 'and stuff' and 'a lot' without precision.

items.prompt:
Is this sentence formal or informal?
'I regret that I was unable to attend the science fair.'
A) Formal
B) Informal

steps: 'I regret,' 'unable to attend' — polite, complete language.
No slang or contractions.
This is formal language.

items.prompt:
Choose the word that is more formal for a class report.
'The scientist was _____ with her discovery.'
A) super happy
B) pleased

steps: 'Pleased' is a formal, precise word.
'Super happy' uses 'super' as slang — informal.
For a class report, use 'pleased' or 'delighted.'

items.prompt:
Which sentence would you write to your teacher?
A) 'Hey, I dunno if I can come tomorrow.'
B) 'I am not certain whether I will be able to attend tomorrow.'
items.answer: B) 'I am not certain whether I will be able to attend tomorrow.'

steps: Writing to a teacher is a formal situation.
A uses 'Hey' and 'dunno' (informal slang and contraction).
B uses complete, formal language — appropriate for a teacher.

items.prompt:
Is this sentence formal or informal?
'Wanna come over after school? It'll be super fun!'
A) Formal
B) Informal

steps: 'Wanna' = want to (slang/contraction), 'It'll' = it will (contraction), 'super fun' = slang.
These are casual, everyday words — informal language.

items.prompt:
Choose the more precise verb.
'The crowd _____ when the team scored the winning goal.'
A) went crazy
B) cheered

steps: 'Cheered' is a precise verb that shows the crowd's action.
'Went crazy' is an informal expression — too casual for a report.
'Cheered' is more appropriate for formal writing.

items.prompt:
Read the two versions of the same sentence. Which is more appropriate for a school report?
A) 'Bees do a cool dance to tell other bees where flowers are.'
B) 'Bees perform a waggle dance to communicate the location of flowers to other members of the hive.'
items.answer: B) 'Bees perform a waggle dance to communicate the location of flowers to other members of the hive.'

steps: B uses specific vocabulary ('waggle dance,' 'communicate,' 'location') — formal.
A uses 'cool dance' and 'tell' in a casual way — informal.
B is appropriate for a school report.

items.prompt:
Which word is more precise for this sentence?
'She _____ her soup without making any noise.'
A) drank
B) sipped

steps: Both verbs describe drinking, but 'sipped' is more precise.
'Sipped' tells the reader she drank small amounts quietly.
'Drank' just tells us she consumed the soup — less specific.

items.prompt:
You are writing a letter to your school librarian. Which greeting is more appropriate?
A) 'Hey there!'
B) 'Dear Ms. Torres,'

steps: Writing to a school librarian is a formal situation.
'Hey there!' is casual and informal — not appropriate.
'Dear Ms. Torres,' is a formal greeting with the librarian's name.

items.prompt:
Read the two sentences. Which uses more formal language?
A) 'My mom got a new job.'
B) 'My mother accepted a new position at work.'
items.answer: B) 'My mother accepted a new position at work.'

steps: 'Mom' is informal; 'mother' is more formal.
'Got a new job' is casual; 'accepted a new position' is precise and formal.
Sentence B is more formal.

items.prompt:
Which word is a better choice for a formal report?
'The fire _____ through the dry forest.'
A) spread
B) went

steps: 'Spread' is a precise verb that describes how fire moves through a forest.
'Went' is vague and too general for a formal report.
'Spread' paints a clearer picture.

items.prompt:
Which sentence is appropriate for a note to your friend?
A) 'Thank you for your assistance in completing the assignment.'
B) 'Thanks so much for helping me with my homework!'
items.answer: B) 'Thanks so much for helping me with my homework!'

steps: A note to a friend is an informal situation.
B uses friendly, casual language — 'Thanks,' 'so much,' 'helping me' — informal but warm.
A is overly formal for a friend note.

items.prompt:
Which word is more precise for a class report about the weather?
'Last week the weather was _____; we had heavy rain and strong winds.'
A) really bad
B) severe

steps: 'Severe' is a precise, formal adjective for weather conditions.
'Really bad' is informal and vague.
For a class report, 'severe' is the better word.

items.prompt:
Which version of the same idea is written in formal language?
A) 'The dog ran super fast across the yard.'
B) 'The dog sprinted across the yard.'
items.answer: B) 'The dog sprinted across the yard.'

steps: 'Sprinted' is a precise verb that replaces 'ran super fast' with one strong word.
'Super fast' is informal slang.
B is more formal and more precise.
